children: on Tuesday said it was releasing  two new AI models, GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol, less than two months after it scrapped GPT-6.1 Astra over safety concerns from its researchers.

OpenAI said GPT-6.2 Astra delivers improved performance on demanding tasks, including scientific research, coding, and the creation of presentations, spreadsheets, and documents. GPT-6.2 Sol is designed as a more efficient model for everyday work.

The company said Astra scored 5.2 points higher than its predecessor, GPT-6 Astra, on the Agents' Last Exam benchmark, which evaluates multistep professional tasks, while costing less than a third as much to run.
The model also outperformed its predecessor on scientific benchmarks, including Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, which tests models' ability to conduct scientific work using terminal-based tools.

OpenAI said it had reduced Astra's API input and output token prices by 20% compared with GPT-6 Astra. The model's pricing stands at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, while cached input costs $0.40.

GPT-6.2 Sol retains the API pricing of its predecessor, GPT-6.1 Sol, the company said.
